Reading this table. The line under each bid number shows only the items that matched your categories — not the full bid contents. A bundled bid badge means GeM packaged several products into one tender; hover it to see everything included. Computers is the exact number of desktops, laptops, all-in-ones, workstations and servers in the bid. For single-product bids that is GeM’s quantity. For bundled bids GeM only publishes a bid-wide total covering every line item (printers, UPS, furniture…), so the tracker reads the item list from the bid PDF and counts only the computers; the bid-wide total is shown underneath. A bundled bid whose PDF has not been read yet shows the bid-wide total with an asterisk* and is left out of the per-type totals. The quantity filter and the type chips use these computer counts, so a bundle that turns out to contain no computers drops out of the default 5+ view. “Bid Start Date” is when bidding opens, not the document publication date. Reverse auctions are excluded — only open tenders are listed. Bids are grouped by month — click a month to expand or collapse it. The view defaults to open bids of 5+ units — single-unit tenders are hidden by default. Use the quantity and status filters to widen it. The page holds the whole history (5,853 bids, also in bids.csv): choose Include closed to see closed bids and earlier months, or click a month in the monthly chart. State (green) is where the goods are delivered — read from the consignee addresses in the bid PDF, so one bid can list several states. Where the PDF has not been read yet the state (grey) is guessed from the buyer’s department name, and central means a national body such as Military Affairs or Indian Railways.
